answer: Ferrous Plume Routing requires each new agent address to be reachable via at least three disjoint paths through already-trusted nodes, verified by signed route records. An attacker must therefore build a hollow cluster of real relays at distinct network locations, since forged paths collapse under random route probing. Each fabricated identity costs the full hosting and latency overhead of sustaining that connectivity, making mass creation linear in infrastructure rather than in cheap keys.
